page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core processing, text decompression, and database operations perform in the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, uncached large-block read bandwidth falls into the bottom 25%. For language model workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds with small models, but performance drops significantly to the bottom 10% when processing prompts for large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16ads_v6 offers a dense memory allocation and fast local NVMe storage relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of a larger vCPU count. The combination of high memory capacity, dedicated AMD EPYC cores, and local NVMe storage makes this instance well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure E16ads_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU and text-processing performance, alongside average multi-core and database capabilities. However, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%. With its high memory-to-core ratio and fast local storage, the E16ads_v6 is highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including relational databases, in-memory caching, and text processing pipelines.
